input.summary: The change introduces two exploitable security issues: file reads no longer enforce the configured root, and search patterns can execute arbitrary shell commands.

findings.title: read_file bypasses root containment
findings.description: The function now reads the caller-provided path directly, so the existing root boundary check is bypassed. A caller can read arbitrary files accessible to the process, including absolute paths or paths outside the configured root.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the target relative to `root`, verify it with `_inside(base, target)`, and only then read it (while preserving the read-size limit).

findings.title: Search pattern enables arbitrary command execution
findings.description: Any pattern beginning with `!` is passed directly to the shell. An attacker controlling the search pattern can execute arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.
findings.recommendation: Remove shell execution entirely; treat every pattern as a regular expression and handle invalid patterns explicitly if needed.
